entries.relevance_notes: Explicitly identified as Legatus Aug. pro pr. of Galatia (Galatiae) under Septimius Severus, attested on milestones of Lycaonia and Isauria between 198 and 200 AD.

segments.name_variants: C. Atticius Strabo t. 1...... [S]trabonem t. 2.... nicium (recte ...tieium) ...banum St[r]a[bo]nem t. 3. T. ATTICIVMNOR. M.... PRAO. NEM legere sibi visi sunt editores in t. 4.
segments.identification_and_sources: memoratur in miliariis Lycaoniae et Isauriae Stud. in the hist. and art of the eastern prov. ed. segments.offices_and_career: Legatus Aug. pro pr. (Galatiae) t. 1—4 a. 198 t. 2. 3 (ubi Septimius Severus appellatur tribuniciae potestatis VI imp. XI), a. 200 t. 4 (trib. pot. VIII; vix fuit VIIIT).

segments.family_and_social_relations: Pater probabiliter eius qui sequitur (T. Atticius Strabo Romulus, PIR A 1332).
segments.prosopographical_commentary: The milestones record his name with some variations and corruptions in the readings of the editors (e.g., T. ATTICIVMNOR. M.... PRAO. NEM).

governorship_factoids.exact_text: Legatus Aug. pro pr. (Galatiae) t. 1—4 a. 198 t. 2. 3 (ubi Septimius Severus appellatur tribuniciae potestatis VI imp. XI), a. 200 t. 4 (trib. pot. VIII; vix fuit VIIIT)
notes: The milestones date to the reign of Septimius Severus, specifically mentioning his tribunician power VI (198 AD) and VIII (200 AD).
Mentioned in PIR A 1332 as a clarissimus puer.

entry_notes: The reading of the name on milestone 4 was problematic for the editors (T. ATTICIVMNOR. M.... PRAO. NEM).

review.note: A 1331 confirmed as governor of Galatia in AD 198-200.
